clue.text: Pass the fish

definitions.meaning: to pass something is to ... it, a two-word verb phrase
a small spiny-finned sea creature found in coastal waters

explanation.definitionFit: To pass a place is to go by it, and the goby is a small coastal sea fish; both senses share the spelling.

clue.text: In age erect as a relatively young woman

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'In age erect as a relatively young woman (5,5)' is an anagram of IN AGE ERECT but has no word that can signal the anagram; an indicator seems lost in OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: In age erect as a relatively young woman

clue.text: First banana skin turning up is a warning signal

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the next word
in a down clue turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: fruit skin is peel

explanation.surface: A banana skin on the floor is a sign of a slip to come.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the skin reads upwards; the surface's slip on a banana skin hides the mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is a short electronic tone used as an alert.

clue.text: Poet whose tools are of value

parts.note: a poet's tools of trade are words
something of value has worth

explanation.surface: A poet whose stock in trade is precious language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whose' and 'are' only link the pieces: a poet's tools are WORDS, and what is of value has WORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet of the Lake District.

clue.text: Don't our characters appear pompous!

indicators.note: the letters of the words appear as new characters in a different order

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some people seem self-important.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund describes inflated, pretentious speech or style.

clue.text: Cast out, perhaps, by the underworld, turned due south

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god and realm of the underworld

indicators.note: turned means the letters are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone banished by the underworld turns south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges DUE plus S into USED; the definition is by example, flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discarded, such as a thing cast out, is no longer in use.

clue.text: Refuse a stew badly prepared

indicators.note: a dish badly prepared is messed up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Turning down a poorly cooked casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is rubbish or discarded material.

clue.text: Inexperienced driver entering the highway had turned left, he wrote

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the driver goes into the road

parts.note: a highway is a road
L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: turned means the short word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A learner driver joins the main road and turns left.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows an L plate. 'turned' reverses HAD to DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl was a British author of children's books.

clue.text: Fury the man grabs at

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it inside, so the man's pronoun goes round the short word

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: An angry man lunges at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate is intense loathing, close to rage.

clue.text: Enclosure built at docks out east

indicators.note: built means constructed, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A pen constructed at the docks out to the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a fenced barrier of stakes forming a compound.

clue.text: Bullying to silence democratic choices

indicators.note: bullying pushes things around, so the letters of the following words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Intimidating people into keeping quiet undermines the democratic vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bullying' looks like part of the story about voter suppression but it tells you to rearrange TO SILENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Polls in which citizens vote are the democratic way of choosing representatives.

clue.text: Little tin lying in the street

indicators.note: one thing lying in another sits within it, so the tin goes inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A small tin can lies abandoned in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, a synonym for little in quantity.

clue.text: Subject to nervous twitch, having had internal operation

indicators.note: the twitch is given something inside it, so the operation goes within

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A patient prone to a twitch has undergone surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' reads as 'prone to', but 'Subject' alone is the definition and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject or theme of a discussion.

clue.text: Reeling, after Tuesday outing round the Nag's Head

indicators.note: the shuffled day goes round the single letter
an outing here is a jaunt that throws the letters of the weekday out of order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone staggering home after a Tuesday trip to a pub called the Nag's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' rearranges TUESDAY to USTEADY, which goes 'round' N, the first letter of 'Nag's'. The Nag's Head is a common British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reeling is staggering and unsteady on their feet.

clue.text: The way for horses and groom heading for church, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals the words are spoken and a different spelling entered

parts.note: a groom going to his wedding walks the route of the bridal party, a bridal path

explanation.surface: Horses on the track and a bridegroom on his way to the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' suggests a stable hand, but it is the bridegroom; his wedding route is a bridal path.
explanation.definitionFit: A track for riders on horseback, where riding is permitted.

clue.text: On the ship? At home, suffering from 25 down, reportedly

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is said aloud and a different spelling entered

parts.note: the answer to 25 down is listlessness, and someone suffering from it is fed up and weary

explanation.surface: A sailor stuck at home is restless for the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 25 down, a word for listlessness, so 'suffering from' it means being fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Inboard describes something positioned within the hull of a vessel.

clue.text: Start culling our herbs developing leaflets

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters are rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Gardeners cut back their herbs and print instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: C from 'culling' joins OUR HERBS and 'developing' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Brochures are small printed booklets or pamphlets.

clue.text: "Paradise Lost", when Adam first leaves, in anguish

indicators.note: lost is read as gone astray, so the remaining letters wander into a new order
the letter leaves the word, so it is taken out
the first letter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Milton's epic loses its first man and the result is grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when Adam first leaves' removes A from PARADISE, and 'Lost' rearranges PRADISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a kind of deep anguish.

clue.text: Melancholic? In this case doctor supplied sour mixture

parts.note: so means in this way or in this case
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

indicators.note: a mixture is blended, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A gloomy patient whose doctor prescribed a sour potion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombrous is an old word for gloomy and sombre.

clue.text: Clothing carrying asphyxiation risk?

parts.note: close-fitting necklaces or collars worn tight round the throat, whose name suggests strangulation

explanation.definitionFit: These tight neckbands are named as if they would throttle the wearer.

clue.text: Exclusive type of shirt or vest

parts.note: exclusive means sole or single
a T-shirt is a type of shirt

explanation.surface: A designer shirt or vest sold exclusively.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless undershirt or athletic top.

clue.text: From behind, came to the fore in disordered fashion

parts.note: one's behind is one's rump
to come to the fore is to lead, past tense led

explanation.surface: Someone pushes from the back to the front in a chaotic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From behind' sounds like a reversal signal, but 'behind' is the bottom, RUMP, and 'From' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpled means creased and untidy, messed up.

clue.text: Upstanding teacher boy found for course

indicators.note: in a down clue upstanding means the word reads upwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
Otto is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An honest teacher finds a boy for a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a school class; it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Taken off by plane

parts.note: reads like flying away on an aircraft but refers to the carpenter's tool that pares thin curls from wood

explanation.definitionFit: Thin curled slivers pared from wood with a carpenter's tool.

clue.text: Are such statistics essential?

definitions.meaning: ... statistics are figures for births and deaths, or a woman's measurements

explanation.definitionFit: Vital statistics is a fixed phrase, and vital also means indispensable.

clue.text: Magistrate dealing with first offender

parts.note: RE means concerning or dealing with
Eve was the first sinner in Genesis, eating the forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: A judge handles a criminal's first case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first offender' suggests a lenient sentence; it is Eve, the first sinner in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with some judicial duties.

clue.text: Low interest rate driving nine characters round the bend

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the single letter
driving someone round the bend makes them mad, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a U-bend is the curved pipe under a sink, shaped like a U

explanation.surface: A financial phrase about low rates that drive people mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving nine' rearranges NINE to ENNI, which goes 'round' U. 'Low interest rate' is a playful way to describe boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is a state of very low engagement or zest.

clue.text: Barrier of tangled wire

indicators.note: tangled means twisted up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fence made of knotted wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam across a river.

clue.text: Bird, mainly green, fluttering to tree-top? It's white!

indicators.note: fluttering suggests wings moving about, so the letters are jumbled
mainly means most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the top of the word tree is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird flutters from the greenery to the top of a tree and turns out to be white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly green' gives GREE, which 'fluttering' turns into EGRE, followed by T. 'It's white!' adds colour: the bird is a white heron.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron of wetlands.

clue.text: Hail a unit in action on the Baltic front

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Saluting a military unit in combat on the Baltic front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a country with a coast on the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Lone suitor changing tack, shows determination

indicators.note: a change of tack is a change of direction, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A single wooer tries a new approach and shows grit.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution is firmness of purpose, steadfast will.

clue.text: Inside rind, stone of fruit gets hard

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit like a cherry
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Inside the peel, the fruit's stone becomes tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside rind' reads as a location for the stone, but it defines the white layer under citrus peel.
explanation.definitionFit: The white spongy layer lining the skin of citrus fruit lies just under the rind.
